subject: Order form: invoice entity split + SLA credit language
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@brightsolar.com>, procurement@brightsolar.com
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order form: invoice entity split + SLA credit language

Hi Maria / procurement team,

Thanks again for the demo last week — really appreciate the constructive feedback on routing and multiregion needs. Attached is our current Order Form draft (OrderForm_v3.pdf). Two items we need clarity on before legal/finance will sign:

1) Invoice entity & split: you mentioned you need invoices split to both BrightSolar US (tax resident) and BrightSolar EU (VAT flows). Can you confirm the legal entity names and the percentage assignment per invoice (e.g., 70/30)? We can support split invoicing but need the exact entity names + PO numbers.

2) Net terms: your AP previously signaled Net45; our standard is Net30 for self-serve SKUs but we can accept Net45 for committed contracts. Can you confirm final term?

3) Taxes & evidence: for VAT handling — will BrightSolar provide VAT registration numbers and a local VAT certificate? If you prefer us to invoice gross with VAT shown, we need to know which entity will bear VAT.

We’ve also got a couple of commercial items to propose in the redline: a narrowly-scoped SLA credit clause (service credits for missed availability windows) and a quarterly reconciliation clause for usage/proration on min-commits. Kimberly / Ben — can you help with redlines so I can return a single annotated PDF to Maria?

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@brightsolar.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@brightsolar.com
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 08:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Order form: invoice entity split + SLA credit language

Hi Jordan — thanks for the note. A few answers below:

1) Invoice split: BrightSolar US, Inc. (EIN: 12-3456789) will be billed for 65% of platform fees; BrightSolar Energy EU GmbH (VAT: DE123456789) will be billed for 35%. We'll provide the exact PO numbers in a follow-up.

2) Net terms: finance confirms Net45 is acceptable for this contract.

3) Taxes: EU entity will handle VAT; please invoice BrightSolar Energy EU GmbH with VAT applied. I attached our VAT certificate for reference (Tax_Evidence_BrightSolar.pdf).

We prefer as few redlines as possible — if you can send your proposed changes in one PDF, procurement will mark any contested lines and return.

Best,
Maria Lopez
Head of Procurement | BrightSolar Inc.

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 11:10:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Order form: invoice entity split + SLA credit language

Team — forwarding Maria's confirmation. Key asks for our redline: 1) updated invoice entity lines and % split, 2) Net45 acceptance (confirm contract language), 3) VAT responsibility noted as EU entity (we should show VAT line).

Ben — can you draft an MSA/Order Form redline that:
- Adds an invoice-entity table (entity name, remit address, tax id, % allocation)
- Adds SLA credit language (capped, service-month basis)
- Adds quarterly reconciliation & proration process for min-commit usage adjustments

Kimberly — confirm whether Billing Ops needs a PO workflow note (separate invoices vs combined pdf with entity headers).

Deadline: Maria wants a single annotated PDF by EOD Wednesday so procurement can review Thursday.

Thanks,
Jordan

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Order form: invoice entity split + SLA credit language

Jordan / team — draft redline attached (OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf). High-level notes:

1) Invoice entity table: I added a structured table in the Order Form (Section 1.2) that maps the two entities, their tax IDs, remit addresses, PO number placeholder, and the % allocation. We included language: "Invoices may be delivered as separate entity-specific invoices or as a single combined package with entity-specific invoice pages; Customer must specify preferred delivery at time of PO." That gives ops flexibility.

2) VAT: I added explicit wording that BrightSolar Energy EU GmbH is responsible for applicable VAT; Redwood will show VAT on EU invoices and remit gross amounts to BrightSolar EU where required. Also added a clause that BrightSolar must provide valid VAT registration evidence at signing (we referenced the attached Tax_Evidence_BrightSolar.pdf).

3) Net terms: replaced the generic Net30 with a negotiated Net45 in the Order Form and added a short late-fee carve-out limited to interest at state statutory rates (commercially reasonable).

4) SLA credits: added a narrowly bounded SLA credit in Section 4.3 — credits up to 10% of monthly invoice for sustained availability failures defined by monthly uptime below X% (I left X% number to product, suggested 99.5%). Credits are the exclusive remedy for availability breaches — protects Redwood commercially.

5) Quarterly reconciliation & proration: added a process in Section 2.6 for usage reconciliation against min-commit and a one-time retroactive proration for over/under usage, with a 30-day dispute window.

I kept language purposefully concise to avoid back-and-forth. Laura — can you confirm the SLA % and operational SLO metrics we want called out? Kimberly — on invoice delivery, ops will need the PO numbers and preferred invoice format (separate PDFs vs one bundle).

Attaching OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf for sending to BrightSolar.

Ben Carter
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Maria — attaching our redline (OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf). Summary of the changes: invoice-entity table with 65/35 split, Net45 payment terms, VAT handled by BrightSolar EU (VAT shown on EU invoices), SLA credit language (suggested 99.5% monthly uptime), and quarterly reconciliation for min-commit proration.

Requested next steps:
- Please review the attached and mark any contested lines in the PDF.
- Confirm whether procurement prefers separate invoices per entity or a single combined invoice bundle (we default to separate PDFs if you want entity-level accounting).
- If Net45 and VAT flow are fine, we can prepare signatures once PO numbers are provided.

Attachments: OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf (redline), Tax_Evidence_BrightSolar.pdf (as provided).

Best,
Jordan

From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@brightsolar.com>

Cc: procurement@brightsolar.com

Subject: Re: Updated Order Form (single PDF) — redlines for review

Jordan — thanks. Procurement reviewed the PDF and we accept the majority of your redlines. Two quick items:

1) Invoice delivery: we prefer separate PDFs per legal entity (BrightSolar US, Inc. and BrightSolar Energy EU GmbH).
2) SLA percentage: procurement accepts the 99.5% monthly uptime, but finance wants the credit cap reduced to 7% for the first 12 months.

I've attached our annotated PDF with line comments and the confirmed PO numbers (procurement will send PO-87921 for US, PO-87922 for EU in a separate email). See attached annotations in the PDF (we referenced OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf).

If you can confirm the credit cap change and update the invoice-delivery clause to require separate PDFs per entity, procurement is ready to move to signatures.

Regards,
Maria Lopez
Head of Procurement | BrightSolar Inc.
